text:
MPC edged up 0.89% today, holding near its recent high of $399.44 from two days ago. The modest gain reflects the sharp weekly advance in crude prices driven by Middle East tensions—Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown after drone attacks this week, combined with Houthi advances threatening the Red Sea shipping lane, have kept oil elevated despite Friday's pullback. US crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel, well above typical levels, and refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, meaning MPC and peers are processing at near-maximum rates to capture the higher margins this environment creates.

The stock's 8.91% gain over two weeks underscores how refiner profits track closely to both crude prices and the spread between crude and final products like gasoline and diesel. With inventories of both gasoline and diesel remaining relatively moderate (206.9 million and 106.3 million barrels respectively), the refining sector benefits when geopolitical disruptions keep oil prices elevated and demand remains steady—a dynamic that has held through this week's volatility.
